svg.title: 5G initial registration, simplified message flow
svg.desc: Animated sequence diagram: the UE sends a Registration Request through the gNB to the AMF; the AMF authenticates the UE with the AUSF and UDM, performs the NAS security setup, registers with the UDM and reads the subscription data, and finally returns Registration Accept.
svg.text: hover an arrow: pause + explanation · solid = request · dashed = answer

g.text: RRC · Registration Request (NAS)
N2 · Initial UE Message (NAS Registration Request)
N12 · Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate (SUCI)
N13 · Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get
SUCI → SUPI, authentication vector
authentication data
N1 · Authentication Request (NAS, via gNB)
Authentication Response
Security Mode Command
Security Mode Complete
N8 · Nudm_UECM_Registration, Nudm_SDM_Get
subscription data: what the plan allows
Registration Accept (NAS, via gNB)
Registration Complete
Step 1: the UE asks to register
The UE sends a Registration Request. It travels over the radio connection (RRC) to the gNB.
Step 2: the gNB forwards it to the AMF
The gNB cannot read the request. It wraps it in an NGAP Initial UE Message and sends it over N2.
Step 3: the AMF asks the AUSF to verify the UE
The AMF finds the AUSF through the NRF. The AUSF gets credentials from the UDM (SUCI is turned into SUPI).
Step 4: challenge and response, then NAS security
The UE proves it holds the right SIM key (5G-AKA). Then UE and AMF agree on NAS security.
Step 5: the AMF registers itself and reads the subscription
It tells the UDM which AMF serves this UE and reads what the subscriber's plan allows.
Step 6: Registration Accept
The UE is registered and the AMF knows where it is. No data session yet (next topic: PDU session).
Registration Request (UE to gNB, over radio)
The UE asks to join. It identifies itself with a SUCI: its permanent identity (SUPI) encrypted, so the
radio link never shows who it is.
On this hop the NAS message rides inside RRC. The gNB forwards it but cannot read the NAS content.
Carried over: RRC over the radio interface; the NAS message is carried inside it
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
gNB = next generation NodeB: the 5G base station
SUCI = Subscription Concealed Identifier: the SUPI encrypted so it is not exposed over the air
SUPI = Subscription Permanent Identifier: the subscriber's permanent identity
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Initial UE Message (gNB to AMF, N2)
The gNB wraps the same NAS message in an NGAP message and sends it to an AMF. It is the first NAS
message the AMF sees for this UE.
New envelope, same content: the gNB still does not interpret what is inside.
Carried over: NGAP over SCTP over IP (N2); the NAS message is carried inside NGAP
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
gNB = next generation NodeB: the 5G base station
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
SCTP = Stream Control Transmission Protocol: reliable message transport used on N2
IP = Internet Protocol: the network layer under SCTP and TCP
Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate (AMF to AUSF, N12)
The AMF asks the AUSF to authenticate the subscriber, sending the SUCI and the serving network name.
The AMF found the AUSF by asking the NRF (the phone book of the core).
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
AUSF = Authentication Server Function: checks that the SIM is genuine
N12 = reference point N12: link AMF - AUSF
SUCI = Subscription Concealed Identifier: the SUPI encrypted so it is not exposed over the air
NRF = Network Repository Function: the phone book where NFs find each other
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get (AUSF to UDM, N13)
The AUSF asks the UDM for authentication data. The UDM de-conceals the SUCI into the SUPI (SIDF) and
selects the method.
The method is 5G AKA or EAP-AKA'. The subscriber credentials live on the UDM side.
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
AUSF = Authentication Server Function: checks that the SIM is genuine
UDM = Unified Data Management: holds subscriber data and credentials
N13 = reference point N13: link AUSF - UDM
SUCI = Subscription Concealed Identifier: the SUPI encrypted so it is not exposed over the air
SUPI = Subscription Permanent Identifier: the subscriber's permanent identity
SIDF = Subscription Identifier De-concealing Function: turns a SUCI back into a SUPI (part of the UDM)
5G AKA = 5G Authentication and Key Agreement: challenge-response between the SIM and the network
EAP-AKA' = Extensible Authentication Protocol, AKA prime: the other authentication method
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Authentication data (UDM to AUSF)
The UDM answers with the SUPI and an authentication vector for the selected method.
The vector contains the challenge for the SIM and the value expected back.
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
UDM = Unified Data Management: holds subscriber data and credentials
AUSF = Authentication Server Function: checks that the SIM is genuine
SUPI = Subscription Permanent Identifier: the subscriber's permanent identity
SIM = Subscriber Identity Module: the card (or eSIM) with the identity and secret key
SUCI = Subscription Concealed Identifier: the SUPI encrypted so it is not exposed over the air
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Authentication data (AUSF to AMF)
The AUSF passes the challenge to the AMF (in 5G AKA it keeps the expected result to check the UE's reply
later).
The AMF now has what it needs to challenge the UE.
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
AUSF = Authentication Server Function: checks that the SIM is genuine
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
5G AKA = 5G Authentication and Key Agreement: challenge-response between the SIM and the network
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Authentication Request (AMF to UE, N1)
The challenge reaches the UE as a NAS message through the gNB. The SIM computes an answer.
The SIM also checks the challenge is genuine, so the UE verifies the network too (mutual
authentication).
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
N1 = reference point N1: logical link UE - AMF (NAS)
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
gNB = next generation NodeB: the 5G base station
SIM = Subscriber Identity Module: the card (or eSIM) with the identity and secret key
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Authentication Response (UE to AMF)
The UE returns its answer. If it matches what the network expects, the UE is authenticated.
A wrong answer ends in a registration failure. This is where a bad SIM or key mismatch shows up.
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
SIM = Subscriber Identity Module: the card (or eSIM) with the identity and secret key
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Security Mode Command (AMF to UE)
The AMF tells the UE which NAS integrity and ciphering algorithms to use.
From the next NAS message on, signalling between UE and AMF is protected.
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Security Mode Complete (UE to AMF)
The UE confirms and applies the chosen algorithms.
Security context established: the AMF can now trust and protect the signalling.
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Nudm_UECM_Registration + Nudm_SDM_Get (AMF to UDM, N8)
UECM = UE Context Management: the AMF tells the UDM it is the serving AMF for this UE. SDM = Subscriber
Data Management: it reads the subscription.
Nudm_SDM_Subscribe (not drawn) asks the UDM to notify the AMF if the subscription changes.
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
UDM = Unified Data Management: holds subscriber data and credentials
N8 = reference point N8: link UDM - AMF
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Subscription data (UDM to AMF)
The UDM returns what the subscriber is allowed to use. The AMF keeps it to take later decisions.
If this step fails or data is missing, registration can fail even though authentication passed.
Carried over: HTTP/2 with JSON message bodies, over TCP (service-based interface)
UDM = Unified Data Management: holds subscriber data and credentials
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
HTTP/2 = Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 2: the web protocol reused by the core for its APIs
JSON = JavaScript Object Notation: the text format of the message bodies
TCP = Transmission Control Protocol: reliable byte-stream transport
Registration Accept (AMF to UE, N1)
The AMF accepts the registration and assigns a temporary identity, the 5G-GUTI.
The UE is now registered and the AMF knows where it is. It still cannot send data.
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
N1 = reference point N1: logical link UE - AMF (NAS)
5G-GUTI = 5G Globally Unique Temporary Identifier: a temporary identity assigned by the AMF
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
gNB = next generation NodeB: the 5G base station
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
Registration Complete (UE to AMF)
The UE acknowledges the new 5G-GUTI.
Registered, but no data session yet. That is the next topic: PDU session.
Carried over: NAS: inside NGAP on N2 (AMF-gNB), then inside RRC on the radio hop (gNB-UE)
UE = User Equipment: the phone (or modem) holding the SIM
AMF = Access and Mobility Management Function: the front door of the core; tracks where the UE is
5G-GUTI = 5G Globally Unique Temporary Identifier: a temporary identity assigned by the AMF
PDU = Protocol Data Unit: a PDU session is the UE's data connection
NAS = Non-Access Stratum: signalling between the UE and the AMF; the gNB only carries it
NGAP = Next Generation Application Protocol: signalling between the gNB and the AMF
N2 = reference point N2: link gNB - AMF (NGAP)
RRC = Radio Resource Control: signalling between the UE and the gNB over the radio link
